text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leaders of bankrupt financial group EBSW continue to do well. Vice-president Algimantas Pashukevichius owes around 30 percent of Cetarium company which distributes Phillip Morris cigarettes in Lithuania. The company had turnover of 65 million litas in 1996.
- The deputy chairman of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party said on on Monday that he was not satisfied as the LDLP was becoming too leftist.
- Inflation in Lithuania in March was 0.1 percent.
- Mazheikiu Nafta refined 1.128 million tonnes of oil in the first quarter of 1997 versus 707,000 tonnes compared to the same period last year.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas said that if all the working citizens of the country paid social security taxes pensions could rise to 320-330 litas.
- At the end of April, the Baltic Assembley intends to appeal to NATO member countries confirming the Baltics' wish to join the alliance and expressing its worries on security.

- Vilnius Bank brokerage house was the most active trader on Lithuania's bourse during the first quarter of 1997 making 33.9 percent of turnover followed by Vilfima at 13.53 percent and Suprema at 10.05 percent.
- To repay all its debts and to liquidate problem-struck Innovation Bank the state may need more than 500 million litas, the parliament finance and budget committee said.
